skill.name: python-executor
skill.description: Run Python code through the inference.sh sandbox with common data, scraping, media, and automation libraries.
skill.summary: Run Python snippets and generate files in an inference.sh Python sandbox.
skill.author: inferen-sh

security_audit.summary: Most external command alerts are Markdown false positives from code fences, inline package names, and examples. Several infsh and npx command examples are confirmed because the skill intentionally runs submitted Python through an external CLI. No prompt injection or credential exfiltration language was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary Python execution through an external CLI
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running infsh commands and show the code that will execute.
Warn users not to send secrets, scrape restricted sites, or access internal network resources.

remediation.issue: Sandbox guarantees are referenced but not enforced by this skill file
remediation.suggestion: Document the sandbox trust boundary, data retention policy, and network restrictions in the skill instructions.

remediation.issue: Executable examples are mixed with many Markdown backtick references
remediation.suggestion: Separate command examples from prose formatting and label executable commands clearly.

content.user_title: Run Python Code in a Sandbox
content.value_statement: Running Python snippets can require local setup and many dependencies. This skill routes code to an inference.sh sandbox with common libraries installed.
actual_capabilities: Runs Python snippets through the infsh/python-executor app.
Accepts timeout, output capture, and working directory options.
Uses libraries such as pandas, requests, Matplotlib, Pillow, MoviePy, and trimesh.
Returns files saved in the outputs directory.
Provides a high memory variant for larger workloads.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated account.
Runs on CPU only and does not provide GPU acceleration.
Does not support interactive windows or prompts.
Network access depends on sandbox policy and target site rules.

use_cases.title: Analyze Small Datasets
use_cases.description: Load tabular data, compute summaries, and save charts or CSV outputs.

use_cases.title: Create Media Assets
use_cases.description: Generate images, videos, PDFs, and 3D files with installed Python libraries.

use_cases.title: Prototype Automation Scripts
use_cases.description: Test scraping, API, and file processing workflows before moving them into production.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Quick Calculation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to run a simple Python calculation. Show the console output and explain the result.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to analyze this small dataset. Return the key totals, averages, and any notable outliers.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Chart File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to create a chart from this data. Save the chart in the outputs directory and summarize what it shows.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Processing Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to fetch approved public data, clean it, create a report file, and describe each processing step.

output_examples.input: Analyze a two-column sales dataset and create a chart.
output_examples.output: The response includes summary statistics, a short interpretation, and a returned chart image file.

output_examples.input: Create a simple video clip with a title overlay.
output_examples.output: The response confirms the video creation steps and returns the generated media file.

output_examples.input: Fetch approved public API data and summarize selected fields.
output_examples.output: The response lists the requested values and notes the source endpoint used.

best_practices: Review the code before execution and keep each run focused.
Set a timeout that matches the expected workload.
Save generated artifacts in the outputs directory.
anti_patterns: Do not include secrets, tokens, or private data in submitted code.
Do not use the skill for unrestricted scraping or policy bypasses.
Do not rely on interactive displays; save files instead.

faq.question: Does this skill run Python locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the inference.sh CLI to run code in a remote sandbox.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create files?
faq.answer: Yes. Files saved in the outputs directory are returned by the executor.

faq.question: Can it access the internet?
faq.answer: The examples show HTTP and API calls, subject to sandbox and website policies.

faq.question: Is it suitable for GPU workloads?
faq.answer: No. The skill documentation states that the environment is CPU only.

faq.question: What should users avoid sending?
faq.answer: Users should avoid secrets, credentials, private files, and unreviewed third-party code.
